newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX at new record after dollar, car rally.
newsitem.headline: German DAX at new record after dollar, car rally.

text.p: Germany's DAX share index pushed into new record territory above 3,300 points on Tuesday, boosted by the strength of the dollar and a rally in the German car sector.
The DAX-30 index of top German shares moved up 45.36 points at 3,309.22 in early trade, briefly touching a new all-time high of 3,310.91, as the dollar was dealt comfortably above 1.70 marks.

The surge among German auto stocks was triggered after after an executive at Daimler, maker of the luxury Mercedes cars, said at the Geneva carshow that the group would report 1996 group profit of at least two billion marks.
Dealers said that market expectations for 1996 profit had been closer to the 1.6-1.8 billion mark level.
"Daimler was very bullish and the car sector is dragging the rest of the market with them at the moment," said one.

The surge in the auto sector was seen as the main reason pulling investors back into the market after a slow bourse session on Monday, when dealers had cited renewed concern over possible inflationary pressures in the U.S.
Some traders said however they were still wary of some retreat in market ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan's congressional testimony on Wednesday.
"We're pulling the DAX up today before we go back on hold before Greenspan tomorrow," said one trader. There are worries Greenspan may repeat signals stock market levels are inflated.
But another dealer said that as long as there was a strong dollar, boosting the key German export sector, the market was firmly supported.

Sportswear-maker Adidas was among the other large gainers, rising four marks to 172 in bourse trade after it confirmed a report that had signed a marketing deal with the New York Yankees baseball team.
Deutsche Telekom continued its rise of recent days, moving up 38 pfennigs to 33.98, just off a bourse high of 34.05, as dealers said there had been a noticeable move back into the stock.
Most said the rise was largely technically, with investors wishing to buy it as an index-tracker running into a a shortage of the stock.
